commentary_segments.text: A transimpedance amplifier for low supply voltages is derived from the differential current amplifier, shown on the left. Only one single transistor has been added to create a transimpedance amplifier, shown on the right. This transistor operates in the linear region, with resistance R . This F resistor provides shuntshunt feedback to the middle node of the current mirror. The input is current source i however, and the IN output is a voltage. It is therefore a transimpedance amplifier! Its transresistance is R itself. F Because of the different feedback arrangement, the input resistance is different from the one without R ; it is R =1/2g , which is still quite low. Since the differential current amplifier can F IN m1 operate at supply voltages below 1 V (see Chapter 3), this transimpedance amplifier can do this as well!
